name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT

  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: tvOS. Top Shelf shows unrelated advertisements that launch a checkout, previews autoplay with loud sound and selecting a documentary opens generic home. Signed-out users see private history from the previous account.

# Apple HIG: Select the system surface before designing its content

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Decide whether the task needs a widget, ongoing Live Activity, notification, Siri snippet or another system-owned surface. Enter that surface’s procedure before fitting an app screen into it.
2. Specify the useful glance/action, data freshness and deep-link destination. Respect the surface’s update, interaction, presentation and privacy constraints rather than assuming full-app behavior.
3. Cover the relevant family/size, appearance, redaction, account and unavailable-data contexts. Shared surfaces require explicit decisions about whose information may be visible.
4. Deliver a surface/content/state contract and preview/check matrix; preserve documented platform support and unresolved source conflicts.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification

name: apple-hig-top-shelf
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting Apple TV Top Shelf recommendations, previews, focus assets, fallback art, and content deep links.

# Showcase content that can be acted on

Read [the Top Shelf guide](../../references/top-shelf.md), including the chosen layout's asset specifications. The procedure is application advice for tvOS.

Inspect available content, relevance/resume state, licensing/purchase context, assets, target platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Determine whether familiarity permits a simple carousel or decision-supporting metadata is needed. Record actual Play/More Info destinations; artwork alone does not prove precise linking.

Favor fresh personalized content or meaningful resume/active content, not ads or prominent prices. Choose carousel actions/details, a sectioned row, or banners according to content. Use layered imagery and correct focused/unfocused safe zones from the reference, not a single arbitrary crop. For banners provide the supported image count, embedded text plus accessible equivalent, and cycling that stops on focus. Supply a static fallback, preserving its nonfocusable nature rather than drawing fake buttons on it. Keep large asset tables in the guide.

Implement content/asset/deep-link behavior or produce a layout/asset-state specification; reviews identify exact unsafe crop, missing identity, or wrong-target defects. Adapt outside tvOS using an appropriate supported showcase rather than claiming Top Shelf.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a streaming app's static fallback includes painted Play buttons, while every dynamic poster opens generic home. Decision: fallback is not interactive and dynamic selection should reach named content. After: use honest static showcase art and direct carousel Play/More Info links for fresh relevant titles, with focus-safe imagery.

Deliver the artifact, chosen layout, content policy, asset/fallback mapping, and destinations. Verify focus/unfocus crops, unavailable dynamic content, consumed-item policy, banner accessibility, and direct launch. Fail for fake fallback interaction, misleading purchase promotion, or deep links to the wrong item. Native Home Screen/remote preview behavior requires actual TV/client evidence.

Load [lockups](../../../apple-hig-layout-and-organization/.topics/apple-hig-lockups/SKILL.md) for in-app focus units or [playing-video](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-playing-video/SKILL.md) for playback continuation.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

For health-related work, finish the domain decisions as well as the permission
sequence. Read [CareKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md)
for care plans, scheduled treatment tasks, or symptom/event recording;
[HealthKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-healthkit/SKILL.md)
for health-data access and sharing; and
[ResearchKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-researchkit/SKILL.md)
for study participation and research consent. These experience procedures help
choose task, data, and consent behavior in the existing stack; consulting a
framework-named topic does not require adopting that SDK. General privacy,
language, and accessibility guidance alone does not resolve those domain choices.

# Top Shelf Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Top Shelf showcases a favorite Dock app's content on Apple TV Home Screen. Full-screen previews can play as the Dock recedes, and people can browse to Play or More Info. ## Best practices Deep-link directly to content. Carousel templates provide playback and detail buttons. Feature fresh, relevant releases rather than already consumed/purchased items, and personalize recommendations, resume playback, or active games. Avoid ads and prominent prices; show purchase information when interest warrants it. Prefer dynamic content and layered imagery. Provide a static fallback when fullscreen content is unavailable: 2320×720 pt, with 2320×720 px at 1× and 4640×1440 px at 2×. The system flips/blurs it into a 1920-pixel-wide 16:9 context; it is not focusable, so do not imply interaction. ## Dynamic layouts Choose a full-screen video/image carousel, a focusable content row, or scrolling banners according to the content. ### Carousel actions Use for familiar shows, franchises, or personal media requiring little explanation. Provide a short content title and optional useful subtitle such as series name or date range. ### Carousel details Adds decision-supporting synopsis, cast, or other metadata. Identify current content near the top; a concise attribution can sit above it. ### Sectioned content row Fill at least one full screen-width row and provide at least one contextual label. Focus reveals labels and remote motion animates imagery. Several labels can be supported. The source's per-state dimensions follow. #### Poster (2:3) |Aspect |Image size | |----------------------|--------------------------------------------| |Actual size |404x608 pt (404x608 px @1x, 808x1216 px @2x)| |Focused/Safe zone size|380x570 pt (380x570 px @1x, 760x1140 px @2x)| |Unfocused size |333x570 pt (333x570 px @1x, 666x1140 px @2x)| #### Square (1:1) |Aspect |Image size | |----------------------|---------------------------------------------| |Actual size |608x608 pt (608x608 px @1x, 1216x1216 px @2x)| |Focused/Safe zone size|570x570 pt (570x570 px @1x, 1140x1140 px @2x)| |Unfocused size |500x500 pt (500x500 px @1x, 1000x1000 px @2x)| #### 16:9 |Aspect |Image size | |----------------------|---------------------------------------------| |Actual size |908x512 pt (908x512 px @1x, 1816x1024 px @2x)| |Focused/Safe zone size|852x479 pt (852x479 px @1x, 1704x958 px @2x) | |Unfocused size |782x440 pt (782x440 px @1x, 1564x880 px @2x) | Mixing image types can upscale shorter images to the tallest row height; a 16:9 image can scale to 500 pixels high beside posters/squares. #### Scrolling inset banner Timed automatic cycling stops when an item is focused and loops after the last image. Focus supports lighting/layered depth effects and swipes select adjacent banners. Supply 3–8 images. Put any text in the image because no external label is provided, optionally on its own image layer, and include it in accessibility text. |Aspect |Image size | |----------------------|------------------------------------------------| |Actual size |1940x692 pt (1940x692 px @1x, 3880x1384 px @2x)| |Focused/Safe zone size|1740x620 pt (1740x620 px @1x, 3480x1240 px @2x) | |Unfocused size |1740x560 pt (1740x560 px @1x, 3480x1120 px @2x) | ## Platform considerations Top Shelf is tvOS-specific and unsupported in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS, and watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Apple Design Resources](https://developer.apple.com/design/resources/#tvos-apps) #### Videos

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-tvos
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an Apple TV experience for across-room viewing, remote focus navigation, shared viewers, or television discovery.
---

# Make television choices visible from across the room

Read [Designing for tvOS](../../references/designing-for-tvos.md). Inspect the primary activity, content hierarchy, viewer/profile model, authentication, and input assumptions. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and use supplied evidence to separate confirmed defects from untested remote behavior.

Rebuild the hierarchy around distant viewing and focus navigation. Prioritize legible titles and recognizable imagery rather than filling the TV with desktop density. Map directional movement and selection from each major region. The focused item must visibly identify both location and the available action through the platform's focus treatment; do not leave essential navigation dependent on pointer hover or tiny touch targets.

Choose the appropriate input contract. Siri Remote must support ordinary browsing; games may add controllers and relevant companion/voice input. Avoid making controller possession necessary for non-controller tasks. For long sessions or picture-in-picture, preserve the person's place when attention changes.

Reduce repetitive authentication using appropriate system integration. If the current system viewer changes, switch to the matching app profile deliberately and preserve privacy boundaries. Add Top Shelf, TV-app discovery, provider support, or SharePlay only when the content/activity warrants it, with a destination that matches the selected item.

**Before → decision → after:** A cooking-video app uses small tab labels, pointer hover menus, and one permanently signed-in household profile. Decision: across-room remote browsing and changing viewers require explicit focus routes and profile ownership. After, clear focusable categories lead into large recipe artwork, Select starts the highlighted recipe, and a viewer change updates saved recipes instead of exposing another person's history.

Deliver a focus-route map and corrected screen/profile flow or implementation. Fail if focus is invisible, a region has no remote exit, or a viewer change retains another profile's personal content. Check actual remote traversal, television legibility, and focus enlargement on supported hardware; a desktop screenshot only supports visual hypotheses.

For detailed movement use [Focus and selection](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) and [Remotes](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md); for shared viewing use [SharePlay](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-shareplay/SKILL.md).

name: apple-hig-playing-video
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting video playback controls, aspect behavior, TV-app handoff, exit context, and spatial or watch presentation.
---

# Preserve playback intent across entry and exit

Read [the video guide](../../references/playing-video.md). This workflow is application advice; the source's overlapping 2:1 aspect endpoint must not become an invented exclusive rule.

Inspect content aspect/duration, controls, resume state, entry/exit destinations, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Identify system-player use versus a justified custom need. Record real transport/keyboard/remote behavior; a poster or mock control does not prove playback support.

Prefer system players and preserve original aspect without baked-in bars. Use system aspect behavior at the source's ambiguous boundary. Keep useful metadata unobtrusive and extra actions close to playback. Honor Space/remote conventions and secondary-audio hints. For TV-app entry begin/resume the requested content directly with its supplied profile, preparing an in-app exit destination immediately so even a quick exit is coherent. Avoid unnecessary splash/detail barriers and show honest loading only when needed. On TV keep overlays restrained and use the documented delay before an interactive overlay pauses playback. On visionOS start by choice in a modest resizable window, never force immersion, and preserve system control space; inline video remains 2D. Watch clips should be short with suitable unscaled assets rather than a phone player compressed onto the wrist.

Implement playback/entry/exit states or supply transport/aspect/resume specifications; reviews identify exact control, crop, or context failures. Keep encoding/dimension tables in the reference.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a TV-app launch opens a branded detail screen, restarts a long film, and exits to nowhere when Back is pressed quickly. Decision: the playback request already carries intent. After: resume directly at the retained position/profile and prepare the corresponding in-app detail/menu before playback begins.

Deliver the artifact and entry, resume, controls, aspect, loading, and exit contract. Verify quick exit, PiP, different aspect ratios, interruption, overlays, and supported input. Fail for lost resume position, baked-in cropping/bars, forced immersion, or a missing exit context. Native media, audio routing, captions, and comfort need runtime/device evidence.

Load [playing-audio](../apple-hig-playing-audio/SKILL.md), [going-full-screen](../apple-hig-going-full-screen/SKILL.md), or [live-viewing-apps](../apple-hig-live-viewing-apps/SKILL.md) as required.

# Designing for tvOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Design for a large high-resolution screen often viewed from 8 feet or farther away, including by people moving around the room. Entertainment, games, fitness, education, and home utility experiences can hold attention for hours; picture in picture can coexist with another activity. ## Best practices - Make the entire interface legible and understandable across the room. Use rich edge-to-edge imagery, subtle fluid motion, and engaging audio for a cinematic result. - Work with Siri Remote gestures and the tvOS focus system. A clear focused item should highlight and enlarge as people navigate so location and available action stay apparent. - Accommodate game controllers, voice, and companion-device apps as appropriate inputs. - Make authentication infrequent and easy. Support shared sign-in and switch the app’s profile when the system’s current viewer changes. - Integrate TV-app discovery, SharePlay, Top Shelf, and TV-provider account support when relevant. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 14, 2022.

# Playing video Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-video) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Prefer system players for familiar playback, aspect modes, PiP, and accessible controls. Native players exist in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS, with TV-app integration for supported content. The source defines aspect-fill as the default for wide 2:1–2.40:1 video, potentially cropping edges, and aspect-fit for 4:3, 16:9, up to 2:1, and beyond 2.40:1, preserving the full image with bars as needed. Its exact 2:1 endpoint overlaps both statements; use system player behavior instead of inferring an exclusive boundary. TV and visionOS add transport actions and informational content tabs; spatial transport controls appear in an ornament. ## Best practices Use standard player behavior even when a genuine need requires customization. Preserve the original aspect ratio without baking in letterboxing/pillarboxing, which breaks scaling and PiP. Add only useful metadata that does not obscure playback. Honor ordinary controls, including Space to play/pause with a keyboard and expected remote gestures. Keep extra actions to a step or two; use transport controls for playback-related actions and tabs for supplemental information/recommendations. Handle secondary-audio hints so switching video/PiP and another app does not create unwanted audio mixing. ## Integrating with the TV app Match the TV app's black transition and begin/resume content directly, avoiding splash/detail screens or intro barriers. Rare required interstitials should allow Select to advance and Play to skip to content. Resume long videos at their prior stop time without asking. Honor a supplied viewer profile automatically; if absent, ask once to establish it for later. Keep Space play/pause available. ### Loading content Avoid a loading screen for quick starts. Beyond about 2 seconds, a black screen with a centered spinner and minimal other content can communicate waiting. Begin once sufficient content is ready and stream the rest in the background; any branding should remain minimal against black. ### Exiting playback Playback exits into the app, not back to TV. Show related details with resume, or a containing menu/main menu when details are unavailable. Prepare this exit context immediately after receiving the playback request so even a rapid exit is coherent. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, or macOS rules are specified. ### tvOS Keep noninteractive overlays small and brief; translucent SDR graphics reduce distraction and image-retention risk compared with bright opaque graphics. For interactive overlays, use a minimum 0.5-second delay before pausing media and presenting the overlay, and clearly offer dismissal/resumption afterward. ### visionOS Let the person start playback, begin in a modest resizable window, and keep surroundings visible for comfort. Do not automatically launch fully immersive video. In immersion, preserve the system's predictable player placement and keep virtual objects away from its controls. For scrub previews, provide 160-pixel-wide thumbnails. Inline video is 2D and should leave window content around it rather than filling the window and implying an immersive player; its controls share the plane. RealityKit video suits splash/transitional effects that need no standard playback integration and supports correct 2D/3D aspect and captions. ### watchOS System playback supports short foreground clips, inline or in a separate interface. Prefer clips no longer than 30 seconds to limit storage and wrist fatigue. Avoid scaling assets. Recommended encoding is H.264 High Profile, 160 kbps up to 30 fps; 208×260 px fullscreen portrait or 320×180 px 16:9 landscape; audio 64 kbps HE-AAC. A poster should represent actual content and invite playback without imitating an unrelated system control. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio) [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) #### Developer documentation — AVFoundation [HTTP Live Streaming](https://developer.apple.com/streaming/) #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

item.text: The supplied interface describes four problems: unrelated ads, loud automatic previews, generic launch destinations, and history leaking across accounts. I’m specifying a details carousel with still imagery, documentary-specific actions, and public editorial content on Top Shelf to keep private viewing history off the shared Home Screen.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > result.md <<'EOF'
# Revised documentary Top Shelf interaction specification

## Scope and evidence

Design contract for the tvOS Home Screen Top Shelf of a documentary app. "'`interface.md` is the entire supplied product evidence: unrelated ads launch checkout, previews autoplay loudly, documentary selection opens generic home, and signed-out viewers see the previous account’s private history. These are reported behaviors, not independently reproduced defects. No catalog, assets, code, SDK, device, or live account was supplied.

Use a **dynamic full-screen image carousel with details**. Documentaries often need a short synopsis to support a choice; the simpler actions carousel is better suited to familiar content needing little explanation. This is a product judgment based on [Top Shelf — Carousel details and actions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Carousel-details).

## Decisions

1. **Feature documentaries, not advertisements.** Publish up to five distinct, currently available editorial selections, prioritizing new releases and rotating useful older titles. Each has a short title, release year, duration, one-sentence synopsis, and recognizable content imagery. No unrelated promotions, checkout destinations, prominent prices, account names, viewing timestamps, or progress badges. Prefer titles playable without a purchase where the catalog permits. Five is a product cap, not an Apple requirement. Apple advises fresh relevant content, avoiding ads and prominent prices, and linking directly to content. [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices)
2. **Keep the shared Home Screen public.** Use the same public editorial feed for signed-in and signed-out viewers; do not export history, saved lists, personalized ranking, or resume positions into Top Shelf. Resume remains useful after an explicit playback action inside the app, using only the verified current profile. This deliberately conservative product policy addresses the reported leak; Apple’s general privacy guidance does not prescribe this exact feed architecture. Minimize the data needed for the feature and handle changing viewers deliberately. [Privacy — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices), [Designing for tvOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos#Best-practices)
3. **Show still images only.** Supply no preview video or audio. Focusing, waiting, browsing, or highlighting the app must not start sound. Play explicitly requests the full documentary. This product choice removes the reported loud-preview behavior without assuming a mute preference or autoplay-control API exists. Image carousels are a supported design option in the local guide. [Top Shelf — Dynamic layouts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Dynamic-layouts)
4. **Use real content destinations.** Each carousel entry has Play and More Info actions associated with its stable documentary ID. More Info opens that documentary’s details. Play starts or resumes that documentary after validating the current viewer and access. Neither action opens generic home or directly initiates a purchase. [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices)
5. **Use system-owned presentation and focus.** Keep identity near the top and synopsis concise; let the platform present and focus carousel actions. Do not paint buttons into artwork. Ordinary remote navigation must expose the current item and action clearly, with an exit back to Home Screen navigation. Exact carousel focus movement belongs to the eventual host implementation and must be verified on tvOS. Design for legibility across the room. [Top Shelf — Carousel details](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Carousel-details), [Designing for tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos#Best-practices)

## Content, assets, and refresh contract

Each published entry contains:

```text
item = {
  contentID, title, year, duration, synopsis,
  publicArtworkVersion, publicAvailabilityExpiry,
  infoIntent: { action: "details", contentID },
  playIntent: { action: "play", contentID }
}
```

Intents are semantic contracts, not SDK identifiers or literal URL formats. Never put credentials, profile IDs, history, or resume offsets in public intents. Resolve the ID against the current catalog at launch. Editorial feed inputs are public metadata, release date, availability, supported locale, and approved artwork; authentication and purchase checks happen only inside the app. No new data collection or permission prompt is needed for this specification.

Prefer layered content imagery. Keep essential subjects and identity visible in focused and unfocused presentations; use carousel metadata for text rather than baking synopsis or controls into images. The installed guide does **not** supply carousel image dimensions or safe zones. Obtain the appropriate implementation template before asset export; do not substitute the guide’s row or banner dimensions. Focused/unfocused crops remain an acceptance dependency.

Refresh on catalog changes and availability expiry; attempt a refresh when the host requests content. As a product freshness limit, reuse a public cached feed only while its entries remain available and its age is under 24 hours. Remove expired, duplicate, or invalid entries before publishing. Do not reorder an active browsing session merely because a background fetch completed; stage routine replacements for the next presentation, subject to host capabilities. Unavailable content is revalidated on activation regardless of cache age.

If no valid dynamic entry remains, provide public static fallback art: **2320 × 720 pt**, **2320 × 720 px at 1×** or **4640 × 1440 px at 2×**. Use an app/documentary montage without private text, prices, painted controls, or “select to play” instructions. The fallback is **nonfocusable**; launching the app icon opens its ordinary landing screen. Account for the system’s flip/blur into a 1920-pixel-wide 16:9 context. These dimensions and behavior come from [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices).

## Interaction and state contract

```text
onPublicFeedRequest:
  choose valid public editorial entries
  if none: publish noninteractive static fallback
  else: publish image carousel with per-item details and actions

onAccountChangeOrSignOut:
  invalidate pending profile-dependent requests and increment accountGeneration
  erase any legacy personal Top Shelf cache and request public replacement
  clear in-app previous-profile state before accepting another action
  ignore responses tagged with an older accountGeneration

onIntent(action, contentID):
  resolve public content by stable ID; prepare content-specific exit context
  if missing or no longer available:
    show named-content unavailable state with Back and Browse documentaries
    do not substitute another film or start checkout
  else if action == details:
    open that content'"'s details without requiring sign-in for public metadata
  else if action == play:
    verify current app viewer; never infer the previous signed-in viewer
    if viewer is needed and unknown: ask for sign-in/profile selection in app
    preserve contentID + action through completion; cancellation returns to details
    if current viewer lacks access:
      open that documentary's details explaining access requirements
      any subscription/purchase is a separate deliberate in-app choice
    else:
      read only that viewer's current resume state
      start that documentary at saved position, or start at zero if none/completed
"'```

An account change during launch invalidates the old access/resume result and rechecks using the new generation. Signed-out playback never reads another viewer’s position. A public editorial title may coincidentally be a previously watched title: it has no “because you watched” or progress disclosure. Completed titles are not re-promoted as unfinished; the public feed cannot exclude watched titles without using private viewing data.

Play prepares the matching detail screen before playback starts, so an immediate playback exit has a coherent destination. Exit returns there with Play/Resume as appropriate. More Info and Play are distinct intents. Preserve ordinary player controls and original aspect ratio; prefer system player behavior when implemented. This applies the continuity pattern by product choice; the guide’s TV-app-specific entry requirements are not claimed as mandatory Top Shelf rules. [Playing video — Best practices and Exiting playback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-video#Exiting-playback)

## Worked before / after

Illustrative fixture, not a supplied catalog item: **The Living Reef**, ID `doc-reef`, 2026, 54 minutes, synopsis “Follow scientists restoring a damaged coral reef.” Current profile B has stopped at 18:20; previous profile A has unrelated private history.

| Trigger | Before, as reported | Revised result |
|---|---|---|
| Highlight app | Unrelated advertisement; loud preview | Public reef still, title, duration, synopsis; silence |
| Choose More Info | Documentary selection reaches generic home | Details for `doc-reef`, with its actual access state |
| Choose Play, B has access | No precise documentary destination | `doc-reef` resumes at B’s 18:20; immediate exit reaches reef details |
| Choose Play without access | Promotion launches checkout | Reef details explain access; checkout requires a separate explicit choice |
| Sign out A, then view shelf | A’s private history remains | Public editorial shelf only; no A metadata or progress |
| Sign out, then Play | Previous viewer may leak into flow | Verify viewer if needed; never resume from A; preserve reef intent through sign-in |
| Feed unavailable and cache expired | Not described | Honest noninteractive static art; no fake Play control |

## Acceptance checks and status

**Passed — document inspection only:** All four supplied problems have explicit replacement behavior above. The specification identifies layout, public content policy, fallback assets, precise intents, access recovery, resume ownership, and account-change races. Root skill, topic index, owning families, routed procedures, and supporting local guides were read; official links are references copied from those local guides, not browsed evidence.

**Failed — supplied baseline against this contract:** The reported ad-to-checkout flow, loud autoplay, generic destination, and previous-account history each fail the corresponding revised requirement. These are failures in the supplied description, not results of executing the app.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance:**

| Scenario | Required observable result |
|---|---|
| Signed out, signed in A, switch to B, sign out | Shelf contains only public editorial fields in every state; no prior-profile frames or cache data; delayed A response cannot republish |
| Inspect feed and cache | No account IDs, resume offsets, personalized recommendations, ads, prominent prices, or credentials |
| Focus every entry and action using remote | Identity/action remain clear, essential artwork survives crops, all actions and exits reachable; no focus-triggered playback |
| Leave highlighted for an extended period; browse adjacent entries | No preview sound or moving preview supplied; full playback starts only from Play |
| Cold/warm launch both actions for every ID | More Info reaches exact details; Play reaches exact film with verified viewer and correct resume position |
| Access missing, sign-in cancelled, viewer changes during launch | Named documentary context retained; no automatic checkout or previous-viewer progress |
| Title removed after publication | Named unavailable state, deliberate Browse/Back recovery, no silent substitution |
| Completed item, no resume, interrupted playback, immediate exit | Completed/no-resume starts at zero; interruption retains current viewer’s progress; exit context exists immediately |
| Offline with valid public cache; expired cache; empty feed | Valid public entries only, then static fallback at expiry; fallback has no focus or pretend actions |
| Focused/unfocused assets and television distance | Identity readable, subject uncropped; fallback dimensions verified; carousel template/export validation completed |

## Evidence limits

This is a framework-agnostic design artifact, not implemented software. No device, SDK compilation, GUI, Home Screen refresh, remote traversal, playback/audio routing, crop rendering, accessibility, or security execution occurred. Host refresh timing, old Home Screen snapshot eviction, carousel asset requirements, supported metadata limits, and viewer-change integration require implementation verification. Public-only publication prevents future personal shelf payloads; it cannot by itself prove immediate removal of previously cached system snapshots. # Revised documentary Top Shelf interaction specification

## Scope and evidence

Design contract for the tvOS Home Screen Top Shelf of a documentary app. "'`interface.md` is the entire supplied product evidence: unrelated ads launch checkout, previews autoplay loudly, documentary selection opens generic home, and signed-out viewers see the previous account’s private history. These are reported behaviors, not independently reproduced defects. No catalog, assets, code, SDK, device, or live account was supplied.

Use a **dynamic full-screen image carousel with details**. Documentaries often need a short synopsis to support a choice; the simpler actions carousel is better suited to familiar content needing little explanation. This is a product judgment based on [Top Shelf — Carousel details and actions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Carousel-details).

## Decisions

1. **Feature documentaries, not advertisements.** Publish up to five distinct, currently available editorial selections, prioritizing new releases and rotating useful older titles. Each has a short title, release year, duration, one-sentence synopsis, and recognizable content imagery. No unrelated promotions, checkout destinations, prominent prices, account names, viewing timestamps, or progress badges. Prefer titles playable without a purchase where the catalog permits. Five is a product cap, not an Apple requirement. Apple advises fresh relevant content, avoiding ads and prominent prices, and linking directly to content. [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices)
2. **Keep the shared Home Screen public.** Use the same public editorial feed for signed-in and signed-out viewers; do not export history, saved lists, personalized ranking, or resume positions into Top Shelf. Resume remains useful after an explicit playback action inside the app, using only the verified current profile. This deliberately conservative product policy addresses the reported leak; Apple’s general privacy guidance does not prescribe this exact feed architecture. Minimize the data needed for the feature and handle changing viewers deliberately. [Privacy — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices), [Designing for tvOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos#Best-practices)
3. **Show still images only.** Supply no preview video or audio. Focusing, waiting, browsing, or highlighting the app must not start sound. Play explicitly requests the full documentary. This product choice removes the reported loud-preview behavior without assuming a mute preference or autoplay-control API exists. Image carousels are a supported design option in the local guide. [Top Shelf — Dynamic layouts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Dynamic-layouts)
4. **Use real content destinations.** Each carousel entry has Play and More Info actions associated with its stable documentary ID. More Info opens that documentary’s details. Play starts or resumes that documentary after validating the current viewer and access. Neither action opens generic home or directly initiates a purchase. [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices)
5. **Use system-owned presentation and focus.** Keep identity near the top and synopsis concise; let the platform present and focus carousel actions. Do not paint buttons into artwork. Ordinary remote navigation must expose the current item and action clearly, with an exit back to Home Screen navigation. Exact carousel focus movement belongs to the eventual host implementation and must be verified on tvOS. Design for legibility across the room. [Top Shelf — Carousel details](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Carousel-details), [Designing for tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos#Best-practices)

## Content, assets, and refresh contract

Each published entry contains:

```text
item = {
  contentID, title, year, duration, synopsis,
  publicArtworkVersion, publicAvailabilityExpiry,
  infoIntent: { action: "details", contentID },
  playIntent: { action: "play", contentID }
}
```

Intents are semantic contracts, not SDK identifiers or literal URL formats. Never put credentials, profile IDs, history, or resume offsets in public intents. Resolve the ID against the current catalog at launch. Editorial feed inputs are public metadata, release date, availability, supported locale, and approved artwork; authentication and purchase checks happen only inside the app. No new data collection or permission prompt is needed for this specification.

Prefer layered content imagery. Keep essential subjects and identity visible in focused and unfocused presentations; use carousel metadata for text rather than baking synopsis or controls into images. The installed guide does **not** supply carousel image dimensions or safe zones. Obtain the appropriate implementation template before asset export; do not substitute the guide’s row or banner dimensions. Focused/unfocused crops remain an acceptance dependency.

Refresh on catalog changes and availability expiry; attempt a refresh when the host requests content. As a product freshness limit, reuse a public cached feed only while its entries remain available and its age is under 24 hours. Remove expired, duplicate, or invalid entries before publishing. Do not reorder an active browsing session merely because a background fetch completed; stage routine replacements for the next presentation, subject to host capabilities. Unavailable content is revalidated on activation regardless of cache age.

If no valid dynamic entry remains, provide public static fallback art: **2320 × 720 pt**, **2320 × 720 px at 1×** or **4640 × 1440 px at 2×**. Use an app/documentary montage without private text, prices, painted controls, or “select to play” instructions. The fallback is **nonfocusable**; launching the app icon opens its ordinary landing screen. Account for the system’s flip/blur into a 1920-pixel-wide 16:9 context. These dimensions and behavior come from [Top Shelf — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/top-shelf#Best-practices).

## Interaction and state contract

```text
onPublicFeedRequest:
  choose valid public editorial entries
  if none: publish noninteractive static fallback
  else: publish image carousel with per-item details and actions

onAccountChangeOrSignOut:
  invalidate pending profile-dependent requests and increment accountGeneration
  erase any legacy personal Top Shelf cache and request public replacement
  clear in-app previous-profile state before accepting another action
  ignore responses tagged with an older accountGeneration

onIntent(action, contentID):
  resolve public content by stable ID; prepare content-specific exit context
  if missing or no longer available:
    show named-content unavailable state with Back and Browse documentaries
    do not substitute another film or start checkout
  else if action == details:
    open that content'"'s details without requiring sign-in for public metadata
  else if action == play:
    verify current app viewer; never infer the previous signed-in viewer
    if viewer is needed and unknown: ask for sign-in/profile selection in app
    preserve contentID + action through completion; cancellation returns to details
    if current viewer lacks access:
      open that documentary's details explaining access requirements
      any subscription/purchase is a separate deliberate in-app choice
    else:
      read only that viewer's current resume state
      start that documentary at saved position, or start at zero if none/completed
"'```

An account change during launch invalidates the old access/resume result and rechecks using the new generation. Signed-out playback never reads another viewer’s position. A public editorial title may coincidentally be a previously watched title: it has no “because you watched” or progress disclosure. Completed titles are not re-promoted as unfinished; the public feed cannot exclude watched titles without using private viewing data.

Play prepares the matching detail screen before playback starts, so an immediate playback exit has a coherent destination. Exit returns there with Play/Resume as appropriate. More Info and Play are distinct intents. Preserve ordinary player controls and original aspect ratio; prefer system player behavior when implemented. This applies the continuity pattern by product choice; the guide’s TV-app-specific entry requirements are not claimed as mandatory Top Shelf rules.
